{
  "subtype": "exploratory_data_analysis",
  "focus_variable": "satisfaction_1to5",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "teaching_approach",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "External pedagogical variable extracted from open responses with well-separated, interpretable categories (lecture, project-based, flipped, etc.) that can be segmented and compared against satisfaction. Distribution is reasonably spread."
    },
    {
      "name": "innovative_curriculum_adaptation",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Ordinal three-level scale (high/moderate/minimal) that is interpretable and well-balanced, enabling meaningful grouping against satisfaction. Associational to the theme of adaptation rather than a restatement of satisfaction."
    },
    {
      "name": "student_engagement_level",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Clear three-way engagement categories with good spread; a plausible correlate of satisfaction distinct from it, supporting interpretable segmentation."
    },
    {
      "name": "subject_remote_fit",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Well-separated fit categories (high/moderate/low) that provide an associational, interpretable dimension to compare against satisfaction across subjects."
    },
    {
      "name": "instructor_responsiveness",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable ordinal responsiveness levels usable for grouping; borders on being a near-proxy of satisfaction, but responsiveness is a distinct external theme. Some NULLs but categories remain comparable."
    }
  ],
  "n_predictors": 5,
  "relationship_informativeness": 0.85,
  "rationale": "All five added columns are external, associational themes derived from the open responses, each with a small number of interpretable, well-separated categories that can be grouped and cross-tabulated against satisfaction as well as role, grade level, and subject. None merely restates satisfaction, and none is so fine-grained or near-constant as to preclude comparison. instructor_responsiveness and student_engagement_level trend close to satisfaction conceptually, but remain distinct explorable dimensions. As a set they strongly support discovering interpretable relationships with the focus."
}
